analysis:
This batch has only two files: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/feature-waitlists.md) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md. Both are documentation. The Swift sources the docs describe (Waitlist/*.swift, SandboxSetupCommand.swift, FeatureWaitlistGate.swift, ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift) are not in this batch, so none of the documented controls could be verified.

Documented behavior that would matter for the threat model if implemented as written: a new provider-to-coordinator HTTP surface (GET /v1/waitlists, GET/POST /v1/waitlists/{feature}) using the darkbloom login Bearer token (A-008). Documented mitigations: https-only, or plain http to loopback only; no redirects; 10 s timeout; 64 KiB response cap; control and bidi characters in coordinator text replaced before printing; join body `{}` so nothing about the Mac is sent.

The gate is client-side, runs before setup, and exits 1 on refusal. The documented 404 fail-open path (a coordinator without waitlists lets setup go on) is an availability and product-gating convenience, not a security boundary. A malicious or compromised coordinator could already control setup. Setup downloads and runs install.sh as the owner (TB-013/T-061), but the documented download rules (https, 200, 1 MiB cap, shebang check) are unchanged here and the waitlist step only adds a pre-check before them.

The doc step renumbering is consistent. It does not alter existing-setup behavior: installed add-on repairs and updates, and already-paired Macs, are exempt from the gate.

No regression is evident from the supplied text. Open questions for any pass that sees the source: confirm the token is only sent to the https or loopback coordinator URL and is never followed across redirects, confirm output sanitization is applied to refusal messages and titles, and confirm the unreadable-pairing case does not let a client bypass the gate in a way that matters. The patch excerpt for cli-reference.md is truncated in file_changes, but the full patch unit was supplied and examined.
